source: scripts/lib/aid-c3-dispatch.sh cmd_build_manifest (ac_source classification + AC-lens fail-closed gate + AID_TEST_RECEIPT_FILE validation)
description: IMP-269: build-manifest records audit_input_manifest.ac_source (plan|final_report_fallback|stub) from which source authored c3/bundle-plan-ac.md, and preserves it through to audit-report.json. Half 1 (out-of-band hard fail): when the run's review-profile.json required_lenses[] includes an AC lens (ac_to_test_identity/requirement_test_drift) and ac_source != plan, build-manifest exits 1 (no manifest emitted) rather than run the AC lenses over an implementation-authored fallback bundle — closes E-064-1_2's silent final_report.md fallback; a non-plan source with no AC lens required only warns. Half 2 (same source-binding principle for test evidence): an optional AID_TEST_RECEIPT_FILE typed targeted-run receipt (command/command_sha256/head_sha==reviewed HEAD/exit_code/passed/failed/log_sha256) is validated and sealed into evidence_hashes[]+allowlist[] as hash-bound evidence at the reviewed HEAD; a wrong-HEAD, out-of-tree or malformed receipt is rejected at build time (never sealed) — closes E-064-2_2's false 'unverifiable' where a real receipt existed but had no C3 channel. Does not weaken the unverifiable-vs-fail distinction; C3 enforcement stays observe. Fail-closed hardening (PM review 2026-07-24): ac_source=plan is earned ONLY by a file under the canonical .aid-o/plans or .aid-o/tasks tree — any other readable in-repo file (a source file, scratch note, the impl's own output) downgrades to final_report_fallback (so the AC-lens gate rejects it rather than trusting an arbitrary file); when the canonical plan is git-tracked at head_sha the bundle is read from that revision via `git show`; a gitignored .aid-o plan (untracked at head) is a canonical worktree artifact sealed into the bundle. The receipt's log_sha256 is now checked for consistency against a named log: the receipt must name its run log via .log (in-repo, next to the receipt) and log_sha256 must equal that file's recomputed sha256 (command_sha256 must likewise equal sha256(.command)) — an absent/out-of-tree log or hash mismatch fails closed, so the receipt is consistent with its named command, reviewed HEAD, and named log rather than carrying a free 64-hex string. This is consistency-checking within the LOCAL AID trust model, NOT cryptographic provenance against an actor who can directly edit the evidence files (plan.json, verify files, the log, the receipt) — such an actor is out of scope here.

P063 Step 4: `aid-gate-runtime-report.sh [--project-root <path>] [gate_name]` is a thin, standalone CLI presentation layer over Step 1's library — it sources aid-gate-runtime-baseline.sh directly and calls gate_baseline_show/gate_baseline_report_json rather than re-deriving any percentile/formatting logic. Given a gate_name it prints that gate's p95/timeout/run-mode summary plus a one-line data-sufficiency note (derived only from report_json's own data_sufficient/non_censored_samples_count fields, never from censored/timeout samples); given none, it lists every gate with at least one recorded sample. This is a DISTINCT, non-blocking row from gate_timeout_policy_block above (Step 3) — it is advisory-only, never an FSM precondition, and never changes orchestrator behavior by itself (a human reads it, decides, and edits execution.yaml's timeout_seconds/run_mode by hand if they act on the recommendation).

IMP-270: a gate-scoped PM waiver authorizes exactly ONE failed gate's result to be reported as `waived` (NEVER `pass`) for one exact (project, epic, run, HEAD, gate id, command fingerprint) tuple — unlike --force, which skips EVERY precondition of a transition. aid-gate-waiver.sh issue writes a single-use waiver bound by head_sha + command_sha256 (sha256 of the gate's execution.yaml command) with a deterministic payload_sha256 self-hash over the 13 bound fields (excluding the hash field and the mutable consumed block); check emits one verdict (valid|missing|expired|consumed|head_mismatch|command_mismatch|forged, forged also covering a genuine-but-out-of-context/cross-run copy) and exits 0 only on valid; consume atomically marks it consumed (flock + mktemp+mv) and idempotently returns already_consumed on replay. TWO enforcement teeth: (1) aid-run-gates.sh only turns a failing gate into result:waived (+ waiver_ref, recorded in top-level waived_gates[]) when check returns valid at the current HEAD+command, then consumes it — a waiver file alone changes nothing and a rejected waiver leaves result:fail + waiver_rejected:<verdict>; (2) the FSM GATES:DONE precondition re-validates EVERY waived row at read time against the report's own revision.head_sha and requires a non-empty waiver_ref — it never trusts a bare result:waived on the report's word (defense in depth against a forged report), failing closed with waived_row_no_ref or waiver_revalidation_failed. Fail-closed hardening (PM review 2026-07-24): when a report declares any waived gate but its .revision.head_sha is missing or not a 40-hex sha, the FSM fails closed immediately (waiver_report_head_missing) BEFORE delegating to aid-gate-waiver.sh — closing the gap where an empty report HEAD was passed as --head and the tool fell back to the CURRENT HEAD, silently validating the waiver against whatever was checked out instead of the report's reviewed revision. All unrelated gates and every OTHER FSM precondition (plan-gate floor, risk profile, cp3 freshness) stay fully enforced; --force is unchanged and remains the only path for genuinely non-gate preconditions. AID-v3-principles.md §1 — the detector (waiver file) is inert without the two enforcement teeth.

P063 Step 3: closes the gap between aid-run-gates.sh's retry loop detecting a repeated-timeout streak (Step 1's gate_baseline_policy_check — block iff the last 3 recorded samples for a gate are ALL censored/timeout AND each sample's OWN recorded timeout_seconds >= the currently-configured value) and that verdict actually changing orchestrator behavior. When the retry loop hits 'block' it calls gate_baseline_mark_policy_block (sets gates_report.json.gates.<gate>.runtime_baseline.retryable:false + operator_action + policy_result:timeout_policy_block) and stops retrying instead of consuming another attempt (result stays the unchanged literal 'fail'; reason:timeout_policy_block + recommendation:increase_timeout_or_background are additive). Without THIS precondition that verdict was only a report field nobody reads before the orchestrator naturally re-enters GATES:EXECUTE for the gate-fixer retry cycle (AID-v3-principles.md §1 — Detector without Enforcement is Decoration, the P026/WAN anchor). check_preconditions now reads gates_report.json at GATES:EXECUTE and refuses the transition (naming the specific blocking gate + its operator_action) whenever ANY gate has runtime_baseline.retryable==false — required-ness is irrelevant (gate-fixer has nothing to act on either way). A gate whose CURRENT attempt just passed is never affected (gate_baseline_update never re-arms retryable:true itself; only a fresh mark_policy_block or gate_baseline's own reset-on-fingerprint-change path clears it). Same override convention as every sibling precondition: --force --reason '<>=20 chars>', audited via fsm_force_override/waiver.

IMP-263: step-verify evidence carrying a binding block is validated against the LIVE plan.json + fsm-state before increment mutates — step_index==current_step, step_id/plan_step_hash==plan steps[N], reviewed_commit==HEAD; a copied/renamed prior verify file is rejected (binding_step_index_mismatch/binding_step_id_mismatch/binding_plan_step_hash_mismatch/binding_wrong_commit/binding_missing_token). Advancement is idempotent + crash-safe via step-transition-ledger.jsonl: the idempotency_token and the current_step bump commit together (ledger append then state write), a replayed token returns status=already_applied without re-advancing, and a crash between the two self-heals on re-invocation (step_transition_recovered) — never a double advance. Stdout is machine-readable (status=advanced|already_applied), never a bare integer. Fail-closed hardening (PM review 2026-07-24): STRICT IS THE DEFAULT — a non-grandfathered run with no binding is rejected without any env; only a genuinely grandfathered created_at (before the deploy threshold) or explicit AID_STEP_BINDING=observe downgrades. A PARTIAL binding (1..4 of the 5 fields) is rejected unconditionally (incomplete_step_binding) — the id/hash/commit checks can no longer be skipped by omitting fields. The crash-recovery self-heal is EVIDENCE-gated: a hand-inserted ledger row {token,from,to} can no longer masquerade as recovery — self-heal runs only when step-<n>-verify.md carries a COMPLETE, live-verified binding matching the ledger token/step/plan/HEAD (predicate _increment_binding_verified); a ledger hit with no valid basis falls through to the fail-closed preconditions, and pure replay (state already at target) stays a safe no-op. IMP-262: standalone, OPT-IN controller-boundary supervisor for long-running commands/dispatches. `run` starts a command via setsid in its own process group and atomically writes a durable job record (id, PID + /proc starttime + child cookie, command-fingerprint sha256, start HEAD/tree, timestamps, hard deadline) before exec; `status` derives state from the owned process + terminal result ONLY (started/running/terminal_pass/terminal_fail/timed_out/cancelled/lost) and is PID-reuse-safe (an alive-but-reused PID whose /proc starttime no longer matches is lost, never running; a surviving tail -f is never liveness); `collect` is idempotent, never relaunches, exits 3 on a non-terminal job (a started/in-flight job is not test evidence) and marks a moved-tree result stale (exit 4) under --require-current; `cancel` signals the recorded PGID so no child is orphaned and writes a terminal cancellation result — and, per the PM review 2026-07-24 cancel-before-PID handshake, a cancel landing in the pre-PID window is never lost: cancel first drops a .cancel_requested marker (then signals a live group with a bounded retry), and the wrapper checks that marker (or an existing terminal result) at entry AND again after recording pid/pgid, immediately before exec, self-cancelling (terminal cancelled result, command never runs) — so a job can never START after a cancel is recorded; `watchdog` answers resume_needed when no owned job is live and no repo/evidence progress occurred within the interval; `redgreen` accepts only paired baseline-fail/fixed-pass receipts at different revisions with the same command fingerprint. Deliberately NOT a hard FSM/gate precondition and NOT release-blocking (no dogfood) — hence severity advisory. The .aid-o/ workspace is excluded from the tree fingerprint so the supervisor writing its own records never registers as drift.

IMP-232: every lifecycle commit (identity, manifest, receipt) uses a temp GIT_INDEX_FILE index (read-tree/add/write-tree/commit-tree/update-ref) + `git reset -q -- <paths>`, so the user's real staged/working index is provably never touched — verified by index-fingerprint fault-injection tests (before/after each fault point), not merely a clean worktree after recovery. Because the isolated commit builds its tree from the WORKTREE files on disk, the entry guard _aid_lc_precheck_write REFUSES fail-closed if the user has EITHER a STAGED lifecycle path OR an UNSTAGED modification to a tracked lifecycle path, and it runs BEFORE bind_delivery mutates the manifest in record-delivery / plan-reconcile --apply (the in-commit guard _aid_lc_no_staged_collision stays staged-only because AID has by then written its own canonical content). An untracked file from an interrupted run — receipt OR manifest — is re-committed ONLY when byte-identical to the freshly-built canonical one (v2.58.2 extends this to the manifest: it is built to a temp first, so a differing untracked .aid-lifecycle/manifests/P<NN>.yaml is refused rc 4, never overwritten, matching the receipt guard). record-delivery propagates ANY non-zero ensure_manifest rc so a refused/non-durable manifest never falls through to bind/commit; a closure-receipt commit failure in record-delivery / plan-reconcile --apply propagates non-zero (rc 5) rather than returning a false success (v2.58.2), while the stdout state line stays honest (never 'closed').

IMP-232: the pipeline creates a durable git-tracked lifecycle manifest (repo identity + manifest committed together via an isolated GIT_INDEX_FILE index) at official plan scaffold, BEFORE any EPIC is generated, so the required-vs-backlog denominator exists before closure and a new plan never waits for a manual reconcile. Enforcement is opt-in per plan and never silent: a plan with frontmatter `lifecycle_strict: true` (the plan-template default, so new plans are strict) whose EPIC declaration is ambiguous FAILS-CLOSED (error_exit code 6) unless AID_LIFECYCLE_MIGRATION=1 is set for an explicit audited legacy run; a legacy plan without the flag proceeds under a loud, logged migration ([WARN] AUDITED migration + a .aid-o/work/lifecycle-migration.log marker), never a silent skip. This keeps pre-lifecycle_strict fixtures and real legacy (table/##-header) plans working without weakening the fail-closed guarantee for new plans.

epic-merge-to-plan's concurrent-writer guard: --expected-plan-sha is compared against the observed plan-branch head BEFORE anything is recorded or merged (:1231), and the same head is re-read and re-compared under the plan lock (:1391) so a racer that moved the branch between the pre-lock read and the lock acquisition is caught too. Either mismatch exits 1 with both SHAs named and no Git action performed.

READER half — wired: aid-fsm.sh `queue-revalidate` / `init` run it on every dependency check. Dependency readiness resolves ancestry against the ref the dependency's queue entry DECLARES in merge_target (plan/<plan_id> while its plan is open, the target branch once released) instead of _queue_merge_target()'s main|master|HEAD guess, which reported an EPIC merged into plan/Pxxx but not yet released as blocked forever. For an entry that carries a merge_target the evidence-based fallback chain is UNAVAILABLE: queue `status: completed`, an evidence `state: DONE` and the merge-log grep are all claims ABOUT a merge rather than the merge itself, and `completed` in particular has only ever been written by hand — a queue entry is a derived view, never evidence. A deleted task branch therefore yields `blocked` (reason no_ancestry_proof), and a declared merge_target that does not resolve yields fail-loud `failed` (reason merge_target_missing) rather than a comfortable blocked. Entries with no merge_target keep the pre-P064 behaviour byte for byte. Branch resolution (_resolve_dep_branch) is a CONTRACT TWIN of lib/aid-queue-write.sh:_queue_resolve_dep_branch — both halves must answer the same question the same way, or a dependent is unclaimable through the queue while the FSM reports it ready. The ref-charset half of that twin is now ONE predicate whose authority is `git check-ref-format` (aid-fsm.sh:_dep_valid_branch_ref == aid-queue-write.sh:_queue_valid_branch_ref, plus a leading-`-` and quote/control-character refusal): a hand-rolled regex on the writer with NOTHING on the reader made the two halves give opposite answers for every git-legal name outside the regex (repro: a dependency merged from branch `_wip` — reader `unblocked`, writer `dependency_no_ancestry_proof`). A merge_target read back out of the hand-editable queue file goes through the same predicate before it reaches git as an argv element.

description: Every P064 mode decision answers from ONE source — the DECLARED lifecycle manifest .aid-lifecycle/manifests/<plan>.yaml, taken only from the target branch's COMMITTED tree via _fsm_declared_plan_mode. All three consumers route through it: _fsm_gate_profile_boundary (gate-profile cap) maps its verdict and reads no manifest of its own; cmd_done_advance (release routing) hard-blocks on unresolved; and cmd_init's plan-branch lineage precondition (IMP-273) now calls the same authority instead of aid_lifecycle_plan_mode directly — the old direct reader failed OPEN (missing yq, unparseable manifest, or an out-of-enum mode all became legacy_epic_release_mode), silently skipping the lineage check, so cmd_init was a third, weaker reader guarding the security precondition while the fail-closed authority only guarded routing. The gitignored runtime plan-boundary-manifest.json is no longer a mode input anywhere. The working-tree copy is a guard, never a source: a present-but-unreadable or unparseable manifest is unresolved rather than silently satisfied from the committed copy, and an uncommitted (untracked) manifest is unresolved rather than an answer. Closes the CP3 finding where the resolvers read independently-stale sources and could disagree confidently. Every cmd_init 'cannot tell' is now plan_mode_unresolved (hard block with the audited --force override), never a silent legacy downgrade. Adjudicated (independent Codex, action A3). Residual risk: an incorrect but committed declaration remains authoritative — P068 must wire the entry and plan-final paths correctly.

An unresolvable declared mode is a HARD BLOCK at done-advance (plan_mode_unresolved, naming the plan), never a fallback to legacy — falling back would route the controller into merging an individual EPIC into the target branch, exactly what P064 prevents. Every 'a declaration may exist and I cannot read it' case blocks: lifecycle lib not sourced, mode root unavailable, manifest unreadable, yq absent, manifest unparseable, unknown mode value, manifest present in the working tree but not committed. Absence of any declaration is the documented pre-P064 default and resolves legacy. --force converts the block into an override that also names plan_mode_unresolved_override in audit-log.jsonl, never silently.

APPEND half — wired: aid-queue-add.sh delegates its only write to lib/aid-queue-write.sh:queue_append_entry, so the append and every later transition happen under the same <queue>.lock sidecar, and the duplicate check is re-run INSIDE the hold (aid-queue-add.sh's own pre-lock check cannot stop two concurrent adds). The write is mktemp-in-place + mv, so a crash never leaves a half-written queue.

APPEND-DOOR INTEGRITY — wired: runs on every aid-queue-add.sh invocation. The locking row above covers HOW the append is written; this row covers WHAT may be written. queue_append_entry used to emit its caller's pre-rendered YAML block byte-for-byte with no validation, while aid-queue-add.sh interpolated six argument-reachable values (epic_id, epic_path, plan_ref, plan_id, merge_target, each depends_on element) into that block with no charset guard, so a single value carrying a newline appended extra `key: value` lines to the entry. A smuggled second `status:` line split the two queue readers apart — queue_get_field is first-key-wins, aid-fsm.sh:_queue_parse_to_json is last-key-wins — and made `queue-revalidate` report `unblocked` for an EPIC with no branch, no evidence and no merge commit, i.e. a queue status substituting for git ancestry proof, arriving through a script. Two layers now: aid-queue-add.sh REJECTS (usage error, nothing written) any of the six values outside its charset (ids by _queue_valid_id, paths by the exhaustive double-quoted-scalar guard _queue_valid_scalar, refs by _queue_valid_branch_ref), and the library independently re-derives the block's STRUCTURE — every non-blank line must be the single leading `  - epic_id: "<id>"` or a `    <key>: <value>` whose value is one of the four shapes this library writes, exactly one epic_id line, no repeated key, and the declared id must equal the id the duplicate check ran against. The library layer is the class closer: it does not depend on any caller validating first, which is how this defect arrived twice.

TRANSITION half — BUILT AND TESTED, NOT YET WIRED. queue_set_status validates against the seven-value enum (exit 2, nothing written, for anything else — including the read-only legacy `queued`/`completed`), refuses to leave a terminal status, and rejects a `reason` outside its charset allowlist; queue_claim_next performs read-and-claim inside ONE hold of <queue>.lock so two concurrent callers cannot both win an entry, and records a durable blocked reason or reports rc 3. As of this row's creation these three functions have ZERO production callers outside the library, its own CLI and the bats suite — every non-`queued` status in the live queue still got there by hand, which is the very failure this is meant to abolish. Recorded `planned` rather than `active` so the registry does not overclaim: promotion to active requires aid-plan-fsm.sh's epic-start / epic-merge-to-plan / plan-merge-to-main to drive them (E-064-2_2 Step 4, else P068). Deadline aligned with the rest of the plan-boundary cohort.

Two blocking outcomes: (1) Compares ranks via gate_profile_rank; active < required refuses the transition with reason risk_profile_below_required (e.g. active='quick' < required='full'). (2) If active profile name is unrecognized (not in the canonical 5: quick/targeted/standard/full/release) and required is high-risk (> quick), refuses the transition with reason risk_profile_unresolvable — fail-closed, because we cannot verify the active profile meets the requirement (E-061-2_6 Step 2 fix). A missing gates_report.json.profile field (no --profile ever used — legacy execution.yaml without gate_profiles, D9) is a no-op, matching pre-P061 behavior exactly. advance-to-gates itself auto-resolves and passes --profile <resolved> to aid-run-gates.sh, but ONLY when the resolved name is an actual key under execution.yaml.gate_profiles (same D9 legacy guard) — an explicit --profile from advance-to-gates' own caller always wins over auto-resolve. --force + reason>=20 chars remains the only override, same as sibling GATES:DONE checks
